newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN CALL ENDS FIRM, NEW BOND UP IN ACTIVE TRADE.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN CALL ENDS FIRM, NEW BOND UP IN ACTIVE TRADE.

text.p: Indian call money ended Tuesday at 7.75-8.0 percent, off the day's high of 8.5 percent, but up from Monday's close of 4.5-5.0 percent on funds outflows from banks, dealers said.
They said outflows towards a government bond auctioned on Monday tightened funds supply and pushed up call money rates.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Monday accepted bids for 30 billion rupees at an auction of eight-year bonds.
Dealers said most of Tuesday's trade in call money was in a 8.0-8.25 percent range.
Some dealers said they expect call money to ease in the next two days.
"Rates should be down to around six percent," said a public sector bank dealer. "Liquidity in the banking system is still good and today's rise is also partly due to sentiment."
Dealers said prices of government securities firmed up in select stocks but were largely steady.
The most actively traded stocks on Tuesday were the 11.19 percent 2005 bond, auctioned at par on Monday and the 12.59 percent 2004 bond and dealers said both stocks moved up sharply.
The 11.19 percent traded at 100.50 rupees while the 12.59 percent 2004 rose to 107.05 from Monday's 106.65.

"The new bond is attracting good interest from those who didn't get allotment yesterday," said a dealer. "More than half of today's trade has been in the new bond. The 12.59 is also in demand as it is giving the same yield as the new bond but with a tenure shorter by one year."
Most other stocks were steady to firm and traded in low volumes, dealers said.
The 12.14 percent 2000 stock traded at 104.30-104.36 rupees against Monday's 104.30, while the 10.85 percent 2001 was dealt between 100.70 and 100.73 against 100.70.
